content: An antidiarrhoeal drug refers to any medication that provides symptomatic relief for diarrhoea. Electrolyte solutions are utilized to replenish fluids and salts that are lost during acute episodes of diarrhoea. Bulking agents, such as methylcellulose, guar gum, or plant-based fibres like bran, sterculia, and ispaghul, are employed in the management of diarrhoea associated with functional bowel disorders. They are also used to regulate ileostomy output. Absorbents function by binding to and neutralizing toxic substances responsible for infective diarrhoea. Methylcellulose, in addition to being a bulking agent, also acts as an absorbent. Opiates are used to slow intestinal transit, but loperamide is the most commonly prescribed agent in this category. This is because loperamide lacks the typical narcotic side effects associated with other opiates.
